_comment: THE FIELD NOTES (2026-11-04; review round 1, 2026-11-05). What people know about each field of a whole-domain control's output, merged by domain_catalog.py into the data catalog (catalog.json, CATALOG.md). Written by people, never by the framework's language models; the user reviews every entry, and an entry stays a draft until then (pytest --review-gate fails while any entry's review is a draft, or refers to an older text revision or behaviour version). On 2026-11-05 the user approved every entry for integration (review state 'approved for integration', by the user, at its text revision and behaviour version of that day): an approval for integration, not a final scientific approval; the gate passes on approved for integration, provisional and reviewed at the current versions.

52 catalog fields, one entry each: the 44 fields of the daily stream (H2OSOI by its top-1 m mean) and the 8 monthly-only fields the user added; plus FIRE, kept only for its caution (row false): 53 entries in all. Units, long names, layers and coverage are read from the files by code and are not written here.

Keys: meaning (plain words, the model's long name tidied, no process story); group (one of domain_catalog.GROUPS); cadence (daily or monthly: the stream the field is read from); how (total or average; it overrides the unit rule only with a how_why); type (flux, state, event, store or bounded: decides how the screen scores the field), with type_why where the choice needs a reason; scale (the physical scale: ratio where zero means none, or no net flow for a signed quantity such as NPP or NEE; interval where the zero is set by a unit or a baseline) with scale_why; percent (the reporting policy, separate from the scale: allowed true or false, with why; anomaly, difference and the screen give a change as a percent of its reference only where it is allowed); cautions (facts about the data that hold for any watershed, never a watershed's outcome); text_revision, behaviour_version and status (below).

STATE OR STORE. A store is a pool that changes slowly from year to year, with a seasonal cycle that is weak beside that slow change, so its drift dominates what a period shows (the screen is to score a store by its drift against the normal years' trend, which is not built yet). A state has a strong seasonal cycle, larger than any drift, so each period is compared with the same period of the normal years, as a flux is. LEAFC is a state: leaves grow and fall each year, so its seasonal cycle is large beside its slow drift.

PERCENT POLICY DEFAULTS. Not allowed: temperatures in any unit (their zero is set by the unit); TWS (its zero is a baseline the model sets); ZWT (the change of depth is given in metres, depth below the surface, positive down); signed or net quantities (NPP, NEE, FSH, FIRA, QVEGE, QSOIL, EFLX_LH_TOT, QCHARGE), whose values can cross zero; RH2M (already a percentage: its changes are given in percentage points, and a relative percent is made only when a study asks for it, labelled relative); bounded indices and events, which the screen treats by their own rules. Allowed: amounts whose zero means none, the percent withheld where the reference is near zero.

STATUSES (review round 1, 2026-11-05). Each entry carries four statuses, kept apart: review (draft or reviewed, with the text revision and the behaviour version the review refers to; only the user marks an entry reviewed), implemented (the behaviour version the code applies), tested (the tests that passed, their date and the behaviour version they ran on), available_to_analyzer (true for every catalog row: the suite holds each field and the access calls of domain_access reach it; false for FIRE, kept only for its caution). text_revision counts changes to an entry's words; behaviour_version counts changes to what code does with the entry (its how, type, cadence, row and percent.allowed).

FPG.meaning: fraction of the potential GPP that nitrogen allows, from 0 to 1 (1: no limitation)
FPG.scale_why: a fraction from 0 to 1 whose zero means none of the potential

percent.why: a bounded index: its change is given within its bounds, never as a percent

cautions: FPG measures nitrogen limitation only: the fraction of potential GPP that the available nitrogen allows. How it reads depends on the run's nutrient configuration, which the catalog shows from the control's facts cache (key configuration). In the verified configuration (carbon, nitrogen and phosphorus cycles, build -nutrient cnp; nitrogen not supplemented, suplnitro = 'NONE'; phosphorus supplemented to meet plant demand everywhere, suplphos = 'ALL'), the model represents phosphorus limitation but the supplement switches it off: FPG_P, the matching fraction for phosphorus in the monthly output, was exactly 1 in every cell and month of the one control run where this was checked (on 2026-11-05: 160,728 finite cell-months a year; the catalog's configuration line names that run and its years). So only nitrogen limits growth by nutrients in that configuration, and nitrogen and phosphorus cannot co-limit. FPG shows the nitrogen limit on potential GPP at that time; nitrogen can also lower GPP through earlier effects that FPG at the time does not show (less leaf area or leaf nitrogen grown in a nitrogen-poor period), so an unchanged FPG rules out only a same-time nitrogen limit. In a run without the phosphorus supplement, FPG and FPG_P are needed together to tell nitrogen limitation from phosphorus limitation. Neither measures the other limits on growth: water (through BTRAN), temperature, light and leaf area limit growth separately and show in neither
